reason: Follows the reviewed 'perianth segment' and 'perigone segment' rules, which map to the member (tepal), not the lobe. A sepal segment is a free sepal, or the free tip of a sepal in a fused calyx. Sepal is right in both cases. Calyx lobe is right only for a fused calyx.

Same treatment as 'perianth segment' to tepal (R2261). Calyx segments are free sepals in some floras and fused lobes in others. Sepal covers both, and where the source says the calyx is fused the lobe reading can still be applied. A calyx lobe target would be wrong wherever the sepals are free.
Plural of 'calyx segment'. Sepal is the safe member class, as with 'perianth segments' to tepal.
The part is a raceme. 'Cyme-like' describes how it looks and is a quality to read separately. The reviewed 'cymes simples' and 'cyme composée' rules handle a modifier the same way.
Plural of 'cyme-like raceme'. The bearer is the raceme inflorescence.

Matches the accepted 'bearing bulbils' (R3091) and 'bulblets' (R3169) rules. 'Bearing' gives presence, and the part is the bulbil. The clash with 'bulblet-bearing' going to bulb (R1584) is a matter of where the bulblet sits, and it is noted on R3169.

reason: Marginal basal cells are not alar cells (alar cells are at the basal angles). Follows 'leaf sheath cell' (R3694): a plant cell plus the moss leaf base it belongs to. 'Marginal' is a position and is read separately (pattern 04).

target: plant cell part of leaf base (PO_0009002; container leaf base PO_0020040)
reason: Plural of 'marginal basal cell'. Same treatment, not alar cell.

In 'sheaths with blades' (sedges, grasses) the phrase says a leaf lamina is present, which is right. On other organs ('petals with blades') the blade is not a leaf lamina, so the rule must be limited to leaves and leaf sheaths.
PO lists 'hair' as a synonym of trichome. 'Acicular' is a shape quality read separately, the same way modifiers are handled in reviewed rules ('persistent style', 'cymes simples').
Plural of 'acicular hair'. The bearer is the trichome, and the shape is a separate quality.
Plural of 'basal vein', which the 2026-11-13 review (C272) mapped to leaf lamina vein. It is also the same target as 'basal nerves' (R2404). Counts such as '5-nerved from the base' follow pattern 03.
A lateral panicle is a panicle. 'Lateral' is a position of the bearer and is read separately. This matches how 'outer perianth segment' maps to tepal.
The part is the flower. 'Open' goes to the flowering-stage context (PO_0007616), as 'in the open flower' already does in flora_context_words.
The bearer is the style, and 'persistent' is a quality read separately. This is the normal way a modifier is split off a part name.

In floras, 'pollen mass' as a part name (counted, with a shape) is the pollinium of orchids and asclepiads. Loose pollen in other families is described as 'pollen in polyads/tetrads', not as a pollen-mass part. Taxon names cannot go in a part constraint anyway.
Plural of 'pollen mass'. In the floras 'pollen masses 2/4' are pollinia.
It is a gametophore branch of a bryophyte. PO's antheridiophore (PO_0030033) is only the stalked receptacle of Marchantiales. 'Antheridial' is only used of bryophytes, so moss context is implied.
A perigonial branch is a moss gametophore branch. Its role (bearing perigonia) can be shown with the perigonial bract presence rule (R1943). PO has no narrower class.
A brood branch is a gametophore branch that serves for asexual reproduction. It is not a gemma, and PO has no narrower class.
Same as 'brood branch'. 'Branchlet' is just a small branch, and its size is a quality, not a different part.
A branch that bears propagula is a gametophore branch. Its role is not needed to place the part, and PO has no narrower class.
'Papilla' maps to papilla cell (C269). 'High' is a height quality read separately, as with 'persistent style'. The part itself is right.

Follows 'cortical cell layer' and 'cortical cells' going to stem cortex (R3060/R3062): a layer of the cortex is read on the cortex. Shoot axis cortex is right here because it covers the stem and branch cortex of mosses such as Sphagnum. 'Superficial' is a position.
Same as 'superficial cortical cell layer'. Shoot axis cortex is consistent with the reviewed cortical-layer rules.

In Fissidens the vaginant lamina is the clasping, sheathing lower part of the leaf. PO defines leaf sheath (PO_0020104) for vascular leaves only. Leaf base carries the 'phyllid base' synonym, so it covers mosses. The plural (R3069) went to leaf sheath for Xyris, which is a vascular plant, so the two rules are consistent.
Same as 'vaginant lamina'. The sheathing lower part of a moss leaf is a leaf base.

PO lists 'free ending vein' and 'freely ending vein' as exact synonyms. A vein 'ending' is by definition an end that joins no other vein (for example, sori on vein endings in ferns). Veins that meet others are anastomoses, not endings.
Plural of 'vein ending'. Same exact synonym of free ending veinlet.
A panicle whose last branches are racemes is still a panicle, the overall branching that floras name. Compound raceme (PO_0030116) is a different PO type and would be riskier.
